## Closure and trust classification

`PijError::SeatIsGone` sends every recorded `Some(reason)` through `render::caller_text`; only the fixed absent-reason fallback remains plain (`core/src/error.rs:115-122`). Thus the existing close-between-prepare-and-delivery path still returns that reason through error Display and decision-refusal metadata, but no longer gives it the plain-or-fenced predicate. Its content is always escaped, bounded and quoted.

The recorded artifact path likewise uses `caller_text` (`error.rs:58-61`). That Display binding is present even though no production `NativeArtifactMissing` constructor was established in this review.

The remaining inspected `line` uses have concrete producer support: registry descriptions use fixed wording/counts; FYI refusal reasons contain a grammar-rendered message id; audit outcomes use an exhaustive vocabulary; schema recovery instructions are fixed or use the operator-configured store path. `StoreSchemaStale.fix` now actually invokes the renderer.

This is not a universal type guarantee. `Adapter.message` and `GovernanceRefused.record` remain generic strings; their producer provenance still matters. A future caller-text producer must not select `line` merely because its text looks harmless.

The independent withdrawal requester still uses `render::seat` (`http/directory.rs:1075-1076`); adjacent diagnostic text inherits the repaired Display. Original round-two repairs are carried forward, not re-audited globally.

## Shared line semantics and limits

The new separator set includes LF, CR, VT, FF, NEL, U+2028 and U+2029. `is_one_line` also rejects control characters. `line` requires that predicate, at most 500 input characters and no literal `[pij ` marker, covering the genuine framing families used in the new tests.

The caller-text path does not depend on detecting any marker. Escaping preserves enclosing quotes after truncation. The bound counts input Unicode characters, not encoded output bytes; fencing is structural containment, not proof against semantic prompt injection.

Admission retains the earlier printable-path predicate and refusal ordering. Report validation shares the separator set, **not** a blanket no-controls rule: tabs normalize and other non-separator controls are not newly rejected. `shown_time` now combines parsing with `is_one_line`, closing the previously noted raw legacy separator edge.

No scoped authorization, queueing or retry-semantic widening was identified. Inherited main #195 changes are excluded from this F142 judgment.

## Proof ceiling

The hostile error match is exhaustive without a wildcard and currently samples all 12 variants. Its uniqueness check does not enforce future completeness: a new hostile arm without a corresponding sample could still pass. The stated gap is real.

Tests cover the listed framing families, separator cases, length edges and a plain tombstone reason. They do not individually execute every separator at every consumer.

The HTTP decisions test still tombstones before answering, reaching `E-RS-NO-SEAT`; it does not reproduce the preparation-to-delivery race. Closure rests on the repaired shared Display routing and core execution. The prior S1 survivor is not reclassified as a killed mutant.

Raw JSON remains model-facing untrusted data. Generic SDK-origin state diagnostics, other notification namespaces and #183 capability enforcement/deployment are not globally certified by this delta.
